# Server (.NET / ASP.NET Core / EF Core)

Run server commands from `Source/Server`. `.editorconfig` is the source of truth for formatting and analyzer style; the binding code conventions are stated once in [`Docs/standards/server-code.md`](../../Docs/standards/server-code.md). Test conventions are in `.github/instructions/dotnet-tests.instructions.md`; AllOverIt helper preferences are in `.github/instructions/alloverit-patterns.instructions.md`.

## Architecture

- Layering direction: `Pot.AspNetCore` -> `Pot.App` -> `Pot.Data`. Migrations live in `Pot.Data/Migrations`; `Pot.Data.Migrations` is the console app that applies them and supplies the design-time factory (ADR-0003, ADR-0009).
- Prefer vertical-slice organization per feature or operation; an endpoint is a minimal API slice with its own request and response models (ADR-0002).
- Handlers are thin: validate, map input, call service, map result to a typed HTTP result.
- Register endpoints through the extension chain in `Pot.AspNetCore/Program.cs` (`Add*Endpoints()`).
- Expected business failures are `EnrichedResult` values, never exceptions, and every failure becomes a Problem Details document. Validate requests with FluentValidation, and do not leak sensitive request/header data in errors (ADR-0012, ADR-0015).
- Public contracts use the external `RowId` (Guid) plus concurrency `Etag`; never expose internal persistence ids (ADR-0001, ADR-0014).
- Authorization uses `resource:action` permission strings, resolved for every request and enforced at endpoint/service boundaries, respecting the existing site-isolation patterns (ADR-0021, ADR-0030).
- Keep `/_health` available and stable when changing startup or infrastructure.

## OpenAPI contract

- `contracts/openapi/v1.json` is **generated by the build and committed** (ADR-0049). Any build of `Pot.AspNetCore` rewrites it (`OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild`). Never hand-edit it. VS Code task: `server-export-openapi-document`.
- **Change an endpoint, commit the regenerated document in the same commit.** It will appear in `git status` after you build. **Nothing enforces this yet** - there is no CI check - so a document left uncommitted goes stale silently.
- Generation is incremental like any build step: an up-to-date project does not rewrite it, so deleting the file and rebuilding will not bring it back. Use `--no-incremental` when you need to force it.
- Build-time generation **runs the application's startup code** against a mock server, so every `ValidateOnStart()` fires. `Pot.AspNetCore.csproj` supplies throwaway values for `Cors`, `Database`, `Jwt`, `Smtp` and `PlatformAdmin` to satisfy the presence checks; nothing connects or sends anything. **Adding a new validated option therefore breaks the build, not the tests** - add its value to the `SetBuildTimeOpenApiConfiguration` task in that csproj.
- The document is written CRLF with a final newline to match `.gitattributes`, so the committed file holds exactly what a checkout produces. It is identical in Debug and Release.

## Persistence (Postgres + EF Core)

- Schema changes are migration-backed, isolated to `Pot.Data/Migrations` and made in additive steps where possible (ADR-0009, ADR-0010). Keep migrations small and focused. Migration generation is a developer-reviewed step: ask the developer to add a migration and review it; do not generate one unless asked.
- Read and write through the feature repository, never through the context (ADR-0011). Default reads to no-tracking; opt into tracking only on write paths.
- Avoid N+1 queries and over-fetching. Keep transaction boundaries explicit for multi-step writes, and open a transaction only where the writes must be one unit (ADR-0029).
- In a multi-step write sequence, keep each write next to the query that produced the rows (query, act, query, act) rather than gathering every query first and issuing all the writes afterwards. The repeated shape stays visible, which shows when a small helper method is worth extracting and keeps the ordering readable against the foreign keys.
- Preserve concurrency and integrity constraints. No destructive schema/data operations unless explicitly requested.

## C# conventions

Binding conventions are stated once in [`Docs/standards/server-code.md`](../../Docs/standards/server-code.md); these are the ones an edit must satisfy.

- After creating or editing C# files, run `dotnet format style <Project>/<Project>.csproj --verify-no-changes --severity warn --include <changed files>` from `Source/Server` and fix every reported violation in the files you touched (naming rules are enforced at `warning` in `.editorconfig`; the normal build does not report them). Ignore pre-existing violations in files you did not change, and do not edit `Pot.Data/Migrations`.

- One class per file (nested types/records/enums that belong to the enclosing type are exempt, as is a marker interface declared beside the base type it marks — the entity-check `IPreCreateCheck`/`PreCreateCheckBase` shape). Default to `sealed`.
- No primary-constructor syntax; use explicit constructors. The exception is a type that adds nothing and only passes base arguments (`internal sealed class SmallStringAttribute() : MaxLengthAttribute(50)`). Prefer constructor injection; avoid static dependencies.
- No sync-over-async (`.Result`, `.Wait()`, `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()`); keep `CancellationToken` propagation intact.
- Extension methods go in an `Extensions` folder; name the file/class `<ExtendedType>Extensions`.
- Feature-specific request mapping extension methods stay beside their handler in a `RequestMapping` file/class and the feature namespace. The `<ExtendedType>Extensions` naming convention applies to reusable extension helpers, not these per-feature mappings.
- Guard clauses use AllOverIt (`_ = arg.WhenNotNull();`), not `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(arg)` (ADR-0056).
- Parameter formatting: parameters start on the same line as the method name and wrap only when the signature exceeds 140 characters. Wrap after a comma, several parameters per continuation line, never one per line and never at the opening parenthesis.
- Member order: nested types, constants (before other fields), static readonly fields (before instance fields), private readonly dependency fields, other fields, properties, constructors, methods ordered public -> protected -> internal -> private.
- Constructors: the logger (`ILogger<T>`) is the last injected parameter. Backing fields follow the same order as the constructor parameters. Chain multiple constructors to one main constructor instead of duplicating assignments.
- Methods: `CancellationToken` is the last argument, unless a language constraint requires otherwise (for example `[CallerMemberName]` after it).
- Allowed abbreviation in variable names: `kvp` (dictionary key-value pairs in LINQ). Add new entries to the rule document.
- Concurrency: declare a lock field as `System.Threading.Lock` (`private readonly Lock _gate = new();`), never as `object`.

## Dependency injection

- A service is registered by its interface: every service interface extends `IPotScopedDependency` or `IPotSingletonDependency` from `Pot.Shared/DependencyInjection/`. Put the marker on the interface, never on the class — the scan registers interface-to-implementation pairs, so a class that implements a marker is not registered (ADR-0055).
- Scoped is the default; extend `IPotSingletonDependency` only for a service that must be created once. There is no transient marker, so a transient registration is explicit and states why.
- Each layer composes itself: a layer that adds services declares a `ServiceRegistrarBase` subclass and scans for the markers from its own `Add*Dependencies()` extension method. `Pot.AspNetCore` calls those methods rather than naming services.
- Register explicitly only where the scan cannot express it: a framework abstraction that must not carry a Pot marker (`IAuthorizationHandler`, `IAuthorizationPolicyProvider`), a type consumed as a concrete class (middleware), or a registration built by a factory delegate.
- Keep implementation classes non-public; do not make them `public` for DI convenience.

## XML documentation

Every public, internal and protected member is documented; the rules, and the reason a `private` member or a trivial boilerplate declaration is exempt, are in [`Docs/standards/server-code.md`](../../Docs/standards/server-code.md) (rule 16).

- `<inheritdoc />` for explicit interface implementations and for members that fully implement or override a documented member; add `<remarks>` only when the override meaningfully diverges.
- `<summary>`: one or two sentences saying what, not how; do not restate the member name. Write a `<param>` for every parameter. Write `<returns>` only when the return type does not already say what the value means.
- Use `<see cref="..." />` rather than plain type names, `<see langword="..." />` for keywords.
- Do not add docs just to silence an analyzer on trivial boilerplate, generated code or test helpers; suppress the warning instead.
